package fixture

// Data for TestPurityCleanSnippet: typical parser code that every rule must accept
// (checked as a package of class parsers/<name>, so nothing in it may be flagged).

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/rbenzing/minutiae/internal/parse"
	"github.com/rbenzing/minutiae/internal/records"
)

var ErrShort = errors.New("clean: short read")

var _ parse.Parser = (*cleanParser)(nil)

var magic = [4]byte{'S', 'Q', 'L', 'i'}
var kinds = map[uint8]string{1: "text", 2: "blob"}
var epochs = [...]time.Duration{0, time.Second}

type cleanParser struct{}

func (cleanParser) read(ctx context.Context, r io.ReaderAt) ([]records.Record, error) {
	var hdr [16]byte
	if _, err := r.ReadAt(hdr[:], 0); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("header: %w", err)
	}
	if [4]byte(hdr[:4]) != magic {
		return nil, ErrShort
	}
	kind, ok := kinds[hdr[4]]
	if !ok || len(kinds) == 0 {
		return nil, ErrShort
	}
	secs := int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(hdr[8:]))
	ts := time.Unix(secs, 0).UTC().Add(epochs[1])
	var out []records.Record
	for i := range epochs {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return out, err
		}
		out = append(out, records.Record{Type: "x", Summary: strings.ToUpper(kind) + ts.Format(time.RFC3339) + fmt.Sprint(i)})
	}
	return out, nil
}
